source_text:
Οὐδὲν μέγα, εἰ γινόμεθα δίκαιοι, ὃ γὰρ ἐκτίσθημεν ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ πρῶτον, καλοὶ
λίαν, τοῦτο γενησόμεθα 79.1240 Ὁ παρὰ φύσιν βιῶν, οὐ τηρεῖ ἐντολὰς Θεοῦ. Πᾶσα
σοφία φοβεῖσθαι τὸν Κύριον, πᾶσα δὲ παιδεία ἡ μὴ διδάσκουσα νόμον Κυρίου, μωρία
ἐστὶ καὶ ἀφροσύνη. Οὐ ῥύσεται πίστις καὶ βάπτισμα τοῦ αἰωνίου πυρὸς, χωρὶς ἔργων
δικαιοσύνης.
Εἰ γὰρ συνετάξω τῷ Χριστῷ, τήρει τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰ πιστεύεις τὰ
μέλλοντα, ἀντιποιοῦ τῆς δόξης τῆς αἰωνίου, καὶ φοβήθητι τὴν φλογίνην ῥομφαίαν·
εἰ δὲ οὐ κατορθοῖς τὰ προστάγματα τοῦ Θεοῦ, μὴ λέγε πιστὸν σεαυτόν. Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις
τῷ προστάγματι τοῦ Θεοῦ πειθαρχεῖ, ὁ δὲ ἄνθρωπος μόνος ἀπειθεῖ, δι' ὃν γέγονε τὰ
πάντα. Οὐδὲν παρέξομεν Θεῷ εἰ τηρήσομεν ἑαυτοὺς ἁγνοὺς, ἀλλ' ἑαυτοῖς ζωὴν
προξενήσομεν, καὶ ἀπόλαυσιν ἀνεκλάλητον τῶν αἰωνίων ἀγαθῶν. Μὴ εἴπῃς, ὅτι Οὐ
δύναμαι τηρῆσαι ἢ διὰ πατέρα, ἢ διὰ μητέρα, ἢ διὰ γυναῖκα, ἢ διὰ τέκνα, ἢ δι' ἕτερόν
τινα, τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐντολὴν, οὐ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοί σε ῥύσονται τῆς ἐπικειμένης ὀργῆς, καὶ
τοῦ ἀτελευτήτου σκώληκος. Ἔστω δέ σοι πᾶς ὁ ἐναντιούμενος πρὸς κατόρθωσιν
Θεοῦ, καὶ ἀρετῶν, βδελυκτὸς καὶ μισητὸς, τῷ τοιούτῳ μηδὲ συνεσθίειν καλόν.

2
orientation: Evagrius is closing his exhortation to monks, insisting that faith and baptism do not save without works and that no human tie excuses breaking God's commandment.
pass_a_gloss: It is nothing great, if we become righteous, for what we were created by God first, very good, this we will become. The one living against nature does not keep commandments of God. All wisdom is to fear the Lord, but all teaching that does not teach the law of the Lord is folly and foolishness. Faith and baptism will not rescue from the eternal fire, without works of righteousness. For if you enlisted with Christ, keep his commandments, and if you believe the things to come, lay hold of the eternal glory, and fear the fiery sword; but if you do not accomplish the ordinances of God, do not call yourself faithful. All creation obeys the ordinance of God, but man alone disobeys, for whom all things came to be. We will offer God nothing by keeping ourselves pure, but we will procure for ourselves life and inexpressible enjoyment of the eternal good things. Do not say, that I cannot keep, either because of father, or because of mother, or because of wife, or because of children, or because of someone else, the commandment of God, for those will not rescue you from the impending wrath and the endless worm. But let every one opposing you toward the accomplishment of God and of virtues be abominable and hateful to you, with such a one it is not even good to eat together.

choices.english: It is nothing great, if we become righteous
choices.why: Keeps the conditional force of εἰ and the present middle γινόμεθα as 'we become'.
rejected: It is no great thing that we become righteous

choices.term: ὃ γὰρ ἐκτίσθημεν ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ πρῶτον, καλοὶ λίαν, τοῦτο γενησόμεθα
choices.english: for what we were created by God first, very good, this we will become
choices.why: Preserves the relative clause structure and the future γενησόμεθα; 'very good' echoes Genesis language.
rejected: for what God first created us as, very good, that we shall become
for that which we were first created by God, exceedingly good, this we shall be

choices.why: Literal rendering of παρὰ φύσιν as 'against nature' and the participle βιῶν as 'living'.
rejected: He who lives contrary to nature

choices.term: Οὐ ῥύσεται πίστις καὶ βάπτισμα τοῦ αἰωνίου πυρὸς, χωρὶς ἔργων δικαιοσύνης
choices.english: Faith and baptism will not rescue from the eternal fire, without works of righteousness
choices.why: Keeps the future middle ῥύσεται as 'will not rescue' and the genitive of separation with πυρὸς.
rejected: Faith and baptism will not deliver from the eternal fire apart from works of righteousness
Faith and baptism do not save from eternal fire without righteous works

choices.english: For if you enlisted with Christ
choices.why: Second person singular aorist middle of συντάσσω, rendered 'you enlisted' to keep the military metaphor and the second person.
rejected: For if I have enlisted with Christ
For if you have joined yourself to Christ

choices.term: Οὐδὲν παρέξομεν Θεῷ εἰ τηρήσομεν ἑαυτοὺς ἁγνοὺς
choices.english: We will offer God nothing by keeping ourselves pure
choices.why: The εἰ with future indicative here expresses means or condition; 'by keeping' captures that purity gains nothing for God, not a conditional offer.
rejected: We will offer God nothing if we keep ourselves pure
We give God nothing when we keep ourselves pure

bible_refs.note: καλοὶ λίαν echoes God seeing creation as very good
Πᾶσα σοφία φοβεῖσθαι τὸν Κύριον echoes the fear of the Lord as beginning of wisdom
ἀτελευτήτου σκώληκος echoes the undying worm

pass_b_english: It is nothing great if we become righteous, for what God first created us to be—very good—that is what we will become. The one who lives against nature does not keep God's commandments. All wisdom is to fear the Lord, and all teaching that does not teach the law of the Lord is foolishness and folly. Faith and baptism will not rescue from the eternal fire without works of righteousness.

For if you enlist with Christ, keep his commandments; and if you believe in the things to come, lay hold of eternal glory and fear the flaming sword. If you do not accomplish God's commands, do not call yourself faithful. All creation obeys the command of God, but man alone disobeys—the one for whom all things were made. We will offer God nothing by keeping ourselves pure; rather, we will procure life for ourselves and the inexpressible enjoyment of eternal good things.

Do not say, 'I cannot keep God's commandment because of father or mother or wife or children or anyone else,' for they will not rescue you from the impending wrath and the endless worm. Let everyone who opposes you in the accomplishment of God's will and the virtues be abominable and hateful to you; it is not even good to eat with such a person.

problems.quote: if you have enlisted with Christ
problems.why: συντάσσω here means 'enlist/serve under,' not 'enlisted with'; the form is 1st sg, not 2nd sg.
problems.fix: For if I enlist with Christ, keep his commandments
problems.ruling: συνετάξω is 2nd sg aorist middle ('you enlisted'), not 1st sg; 'with Christ' misrepresents dative of association/service.

edits.old: if you have enlisted with Christ

fixed: Changed 'if you have enlisted with Christ' to 'if I enlist with Christ' because the source form συνετάξω is first-person singular, not second-person.

problems.quote: For if I enlist with Christ, keep his commandments
problems.source_quote: Εἰ γὰρ συνετάξω τῷ Χριστῷ, τήρει τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Source has 2nd person singular throughout; English switches to 1st person 'I enlist' then imperative 'keep', confusing agency and addressee.
problems.fix: For if you enlist with Christ, keep his commandments

problems.quote: For if I enlist with Christ, keep his commandments;
problems.source_quote: Εἰ γὰρ συνετάξω τῷ Χριστῷ, τήρει τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ
problems.why: συνετάξω means 'enlist' (military metaphor), but the English 'if I enlist... keep' is ungrammatical: the main clause 'keep' has no subject.
problems.fix: If I have enlisted with Christ, keep his commandments.
problems.ruling: συνετάξω is 1st person aorist, but 'keep' is imperative with no subject; ungrammatical Greek-to-English mapping.

edits.old: For if I enlist with Christ, keep his commandments;
edits.new: For if you enlist with Christ, keep his commandments;

fixed: Changed 'I enlist' to 'you enlist' to match the source's second person singular (συνετάξω ... τήρει), keeping the imperative 'keep' addressed to the same 'you'.

last_rejected.why: κατορθωσις means 'accomplishment/fulfillment'; 'will' adds meaning not in source.
last_rejected.ruling: κατόρθωσις here means 'right doing/virtue'; 'God's will' captures περὶ Θεοῦ context acceptably.

last_rejected.quote: All wisdom is to fear the Lord
last_rejected.why: Greek is command 'fear the Lord,' not infinitive 'is to fear.'
last_rejected.ruling: Πᾶσα σοφία φοβεῖσθαι τὸν Κύριον: infinitive with subject accusative is standard for 'is to fear'; meaning preserved.

last_rejected.why: Greek says 'do not say [that] you are faithful,' not 'call yourself faithful.'
last_rejected.fix: do not say you are faithful
last_rejected.ruling: μὴ λέγε πιστὸν σεαυτόν means 'do not call yourself faithful'; λέγε + predicate accusative is normal idiom.
